                  <ns0:p>AND the LORD said unto Joshua, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 1. 2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>. & 7. 18.</ns0:note> Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple of war with thee <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Partly, to strengthen them against those fears which their late Defeat had wrought in them; and partly that all of them might be partakers of this first spoil, and thereby be encouraged to proceed in their work. The weak multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude were not to go, because they might have hindred them in the following Stratagem; and it was but fit that the Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />litary men who run the greatest hazards, should have the Precedency and Priviledg in the spoils.</ns0:note>, and arise, go up to Ai: see, I have given into thine hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And thou shall do to Ai <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">i. e. The City and people of <ns0:hi>Ai.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> and her King, as thou didst unto <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6. 21.</ns0:note> Jericho and her King <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">i. e. Overcome and destroy them. This was enjoyned partly to chastise their last Insolence, and the Triumphs and Blasphemies which doubt<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />less their success produced: and partly to revive the dread and terrour which had been impressed upon the <ns0:hi>Canaanites</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />richo's</ns0:hi> ruine, and had been much abated by the late success of <ns0:hi>Ai,</ns0:hi> and their confidence and expectation of further and greater success.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 20. 14.</ns0:note> only the spoil thereof, and the cattel thereof, shall ye take for a prey unto your selves: lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up against Ai <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">i. e. To consider and conclude about this Expedition of going up against <ns0:hi>Ai;</ns0:hi> not as if all the people of war did actually go up, which was both unnecessary and burdensom, and might hinder their following design: but it seems to be resolved by <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> and all the Council of War, That the 30000. here following should be selected for the Enterprize. Either, 1. the 30000. now mentioned; Or, 2. part of them; to wit, such as were to lie in wait, as seems most probable both from the next verse, which limits it to those who were <ns0:hi>to lie in wait,</ns0:hi> and from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. where what is here mentioned only by antici<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pation, is actually put in execution; and it is said of them that were <ns0:hi>sent forth,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>they went to lie in ambush,</ns0:hi> and did so; and these were only 5000. men, as is expressed, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. And the only inconvenience of this Exposition is, That the Pronoun Relative <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> is put without, or before its Antecedent, which is left to be gathered out of the following words, which is not unusual in the Hebrew Tongue, as plainly appears from <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 14. 19. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 18, 9. and 24. 17. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 87. 1. and 105. 19. and 114. 2. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 7. 8. and 14. 26.</ns0:note>: and Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour, and sent them a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way by night.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And he commanded them <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The same party last spoken of <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. even the 5000. mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. This historical Narration seems obscure and intricate, and at first view to make three parties, one of 30000. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. one of 5000. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. which may seem to be two se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veral Ambushes; and a third of all the people, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5, 11. But if it be more narrowly and considerately observed, it will appear, that there are only two parties ingaged in the taking of <ns0:hi>Ai,</ns0:hi> and but one Ambush, as plainly appears by comparing <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. (which manifestly speaks of that party which is mention<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3.) with <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. which speaks only of 5000. which is justly supposed to be a part of those 30000. named <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. and that part which was to lie in ambush; unless we will suppose that there were two Ambushes, one of 30000. and the other of 5000. both lying in wait in the same quarter, even <ns0:hi>between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai,</ns0:hi> the only place where the Ambush lay, as is said both <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. and 12, 13. which seems absurd and incredible. And besides, in the execution of this Command, there is mention but of one Ambush <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12, 13, 14, 19. and they are said to consist only of 5000. <ns0:hi>v</ns0:hi> 12. and they only take and burn the City, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 19. so that the other supposed Ambush of 30000. is perfectly vanished and lost, and did no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing in this work; which also is very improbable. And there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, that 30000. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. are the same who are called <ns0:hi>the people,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>the people of war that were with Ioshua, v.</ns0:hi> 5, 11, which pitched on the North-side of <ns0:hi>Ai, v.</ns0:hi> 11, 13. as the Am<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bush did on the west-side; but for any other side of the City, or a third party placed elsewhere about <ns0:hi>Ai,</ns0:hi> we read not one word; and therefore it may well be presumed there were no more imployed to take it.</ns0:note>, saying, Behold, ye shall lie in wait against the city, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> behind the city: go not very far from the city, but be ye all ready:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And I, and all the people that are <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> shall be: for at present he sent them away, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. but the next morning followed them, and joyned himself with them, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10, 11.</ns0:note> with me, will approach unto the city: and it shall come to pass, when they come out against us, as at the first, that we <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">I and the 25000. with me.</ns0:note> will flee before them</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:177" />6 (For they will come out after us) till we † have drawn them from the city; for they will say,<ns0:note place="margin">‡ Heb. <ns0:hi>pulled.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> They flee before us, as at the first: therefore we will flee before them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 Then ye shall rise up from the ambush <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">To wit, upon the signal given, of which <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18.</ns0:note>, and seize upon the city: for the LORD your God will deliver ir into your hand.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And it shall be when ye have taken the city, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> ye shall set the city on fire <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">To wit, part of it, as a sign to their Brethren of their success; for the whole City was not burnt now, but after<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards; as is said <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28.</ns0:note>: according to the commandment of the LORD shall ye do. See, I have commanded you.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 Joshua therefore sent them <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The same party designed by the Pronoun <ns0:hi>them, v.</ns0:hi> 3. of which see the Notes there.</ns0:note> forth, and they went to lie in ambush, and abode between Bethel and Ai, on the west-side of Ai: but Joshua lodged that night among the people <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>that people,</ns0:hi> to wit, <ns0:hi>the people of war,</ns0:hi> as they are called, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. to wit, the main bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy of that host consisting of 30000.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And Joshua rose up early in the morning, and numbred the people <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>that people,</ns0:hi> not all the people of <ns0:hi>Israel;</ns0:hi> which was needless, and required more time than could now be spared; but the rest of that host of 30000. whereof 5000. were sent away; and now the remainder are numbred, partly to see whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther some of them had not withdrawn themselves, taking the advantage of the night, and of the design of laying an Am<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bush; and partly that it might be evident, that this work was done without any loss of men, and thereby they might be en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />couraged to trust in God, and to proceed vigorously and reso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lutely in their work.</ns0:note>, and went up; he, and the elders of Israel <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Either, 1. the military Elders, the chief Commanders of his Army. But they seem to be inclu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded in the 30000. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. which are supposed to be furnished and led by their several Commanders; and such persons are scarce ever called <ns0:hi>the Elders of Israel.</ns0:hi> Or rather, 2. the chief Magistrates and Rulers of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> under <ns0:hi>Ioshua,</ns0:hi> who are commonly so called; and these, I suppose, went with <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shua,</ns0:hi> and with the Army, to take care that the Cattel and the Spoil of the City, which was given by God to all <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> for a prey, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2, 27. might be justly and equally divided be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tween those that went to battel, and the rest of the people, according to the Example and Prescript, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 31. 27. and that they who were present and assistant in the taking of that City, might not ingross the whole to themselves, as is usual for Soldiers in those cases to do.</ns0:note>, before the people to Ai.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And all the people, <ns0:hi>even the people</ns0:hi> of war that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">To wit, the 30000. mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. or the most of them.</ns0:note>, went up, and drewnigh, and came before the city, and pitched on the north-side of Ai: now <ns0:hi>there was</ns0:hi> a valley between them and Ai.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And he took <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Or rather, <ns0:hi>but he had taken,</ns0:hi> to wit, out of the said number of 30000. for this is added by way of Recapitulation and further Explication of what is said in general, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9.</ns0:note> about five thousand men, and set them to lie in ambush between Bethel, and Ai, on the west-side † of the city.<ns0:note place="margin">‡ Or, <ns0:hi>of Ai.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And when they had set the people, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> all the host that <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> on the north-side of the city, and † their<ns0:note place="margin">‡ Heb. <ns0:hi>their lying in wait.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> liers in wait on the west of the city: Joshua went <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">To wit, accompanied with a small part of the host now mentioned, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Very early in the morning, <ns0:hi>when it was yet dark,</ns0:hi> as is said in a like case, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 20. 1. whence it is here called <ns0:hi>Night,</ns0:hi> though it was <ns0:hi>early in the mor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning,</ns0:hi> as is said, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10. for it seems most probable, that all was done in one Nights space, and in this manner; <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> sends away the Ambush <ns0:hi>by night, v.</ns0:hi> 3. and lodgeth that night with 25000 men, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. not far from the city. But not able nor wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling to sleep all night, he rises very early, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. and numbers his men, which by the help of the several Officers was quick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly done, and so immediately leads them towards <ns0:hi>Ai;</ns0:hi> and while it was yet duskish or night, he goes into the midst of the valley, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 13. and when the day dawns he is discovered by the King and people of <ns0:hi>Ai,</ns0:hi> who thereupon <ns0:hi>rose up early</ns0:hi> to fight with them, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. Though others conceive this was the second night, and so the Ambush had lain hid a night and a day together. But then there might be danger of their be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing discovered, although that danger may seem to be the less, because <ns0:hi>Ai</ns0:hi> might be shut up, that none might go out nor come in, but by Order, and upon Necessity, because of the nearness of their Enemies, as <ns0:hi>Iericho</ns0:hi> formerly was for the same reason, <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 6. 1.</ns0:note> that night into the midst of the valley <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Which was near the City, thereby to allure them forth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And it came to pass when the king of Ai saw <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> that they hasted, and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battel, he, and all his people <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">To wit, all his men of war, for the rest were left in <ns0:hi>Ai, v.</ns0:hi> 16.</ns0:note>, at a time appointed <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">At a certain hour agreed upon between the King and People of <ns0:hi>Ai,</ns0:hi> and of <ns0:hi>Bethel</ns0:hi> too, who were their Confederates in this Enterprize, as it may seem from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. Possibly they might appoint the same hour of the day on which they had fought against <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> with such good success, looking upon it as a lucky hour.</ns0:note>, before the plain <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">i. e. Towards or in sight of that plain or valley in which the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> were, that so they might put themselves in Battel-array.</ns0:note>, but he wist not that <ns0:hi>there were</ns0:hi> liers in ambush against him <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The former success having made him more careless and secure, as is usual in such Cases, God also blinding his mind, and infatuating him, as he useth to do with those which he intends to destroy.</ns0:note>, behind the city.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">i. e. Fled from them, as it were for fear of a second blow: and peradventure some of them might be wounded, though none were killed; and might make that the pretence of their fleeing away.</ns0:note>, and fled by the way of the wilderness <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Which lay between <ns0:hi>Ai</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iericho,</ns0:hi> whither they now seemed to flee.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 And all the people <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">To wit, all that were able to bear Arms, for old men and Children were unfit for the pursuit or fight; and that they were yet left, may seem from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24, 25.</ns0:note> that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> in Ai, were called together to pursue after them, and they pursued after Joshua, and were drawn away from the city.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And there was not a man <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">To wit, fit for war.</ns0:note> left in Ai, or Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thel <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Which, being a neighbouring City, and incouraged by the former success, had sent some Forces to assist them; and now, upon notice sent to them of the flight of their common Enemies, or upon some other sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal given, which might easily be done, having been appointed before-hand, as is usual in such Cases, all their men of War joyn with those of <ns0:hi>Ai</ns0:hi> in the pursuit.</ns0:note>, that went not out after Israel: and they left the city open, and pursued after Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And the LORD said unto Joshua, Stretch out the spear <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>thy banner:</ns0:hi> or there might be some Banner in the end of his Spear. This was prescribed and practised, either 1. for a sign to his Host present with him, to stop their flight, and make head against the pursuers: Or 2. for a signal to the liers in wait, as may seem from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 19. who, though they were at some distance, might know this from persons whom they had set in some high and convenient places to observe <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi>'s motion, and to give notice from one to another, and that speedily, as is common in such cases, until it came to the whole ambush: Or 3. as a mystical token of Gods presence and assistance with them, and of their Victory; or as a mean by Gods appoint<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment contributing to their good success, as the like posture of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> lifting up his hands was, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 17. 11, 12. which may be the reason why he continued this posture till the Enemies were all destroyed, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 26. whereas if it had been a signal only, it was sufficient to do it for a little while. I know no reason why all these ends might not be joyned together.</ns0:note>, that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in thy hand toward Ai, for I will give it into thine hand. And Joshua stretched out the spear that <ns0:hi>he had</ns0:hi> in his hand toward the city.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And the ambush arose quickly out of their place, and they ran assoon as he had stretched out his hand: and they entred into the city, and took it, and hasted, and set the city <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">i. e. Not all of it, as appears both from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28. and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause then they had lost that Prey which God had allowed them; but some part of it, enough to raise a smoke, and give notice to their Brethren of their success.</ns0:note> on fire.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:177" />20 And when the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and behold, the smoak of the city ascend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed up to heaven, and they had no <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> Hand.</ns0:note> power <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>place,</ns0:hi> for so the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> word is oft used, as <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 2. 17. <ns0:hi>Neh.</ns0:hi> 7. 4. <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 37. 7. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 104. 25. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 22. 18. and 56. 5.</ns0:note> to flee this way, or that way, and the people that fled to the wilderness, turned back upon the pursuers.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And when Joshua and all Israel <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> All the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> there present, or all those who seemed to flee away before.</ns0:note> saw that the ambush had taken the city, and that the smoak of the city ascended, then they turned again, and slew the men of Ai.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 And the other <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">They who lay in Ambush.</ns0:note> issued out of the city against them, so they were in the midst of Israel, some on this side, and some on that side, and they smote them so that they <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 7. 2.</ns0:note> let none of them remain or es<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cape <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">So their late success was a real mischief to them, as being the occasion of their to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tal ruine.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 And the king of Ai they took alive <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Reserving him to a peculiar and more ignominious pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishment, for the terror of the other Kings, who were the chief causes of all that opposition and disturbance<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which <ns0:hi>Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael</ns0:hi> met with in gaining the Possession of the Promised Land.</ns0:note>, and brought him to Joshua.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 And it came to pass when Israel had made an end of slaying all the inhabitants of Ai, in the field, in the wilderness wherein they chased them<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>when</ns0:hi> they were all fallen on the edg of the sword, until they were consumed, that all the Israelites returned unto Ai, and smote it <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Inhabitants of it, the <ns0:hi>men,</ns0:hi> who through age or infirmity were unfit for War, and <ns0:hi>the women,</ns0:hi> v. 25.</ns0:note> with the edg of the sword.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 And <ns0:hi>so</ns0:hi> it was, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> all that fell that day, both of men and women, <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> twelve thousand, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> all the men of Ai <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Not strictly, but largely so called, who were now in <ns0:hi>Ai,</ns0:hi> either as constant and settled Inhabitants, or as Sojourners and such as came to them for their help, such as being con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sederate with them, are esteemed as one with them; for it is evident that <ns0:hi>the men of Bethel</ns0:hi> are included in this number, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17. the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> who took this number, being unable to distinguish who belonged to the one City, and who to the other.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="30">30 Then <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">To wit, after the taking of <ns0:hi>Ai.</ns0:hi> For they were obliged to do this, when they were brought over <ns0:hi>Iordan</ns0:hi> into the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan, Deut.</ns0:hi> 11. 29. and 27, 2, 3. which is not to be understood strictly, as if it were to be done the same mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment or day; for it is manifest they were first to be Circum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cised, and to eat the Passover, which they did, and which was the work of some days; but as soon as they had opportunity to do it, which was now when these two great Frontier Cities were taken and destroyed, and thereby the Coast cleared, and the bordering people under great consternation and confusion, that all the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> might securely march thither. And in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed this work was fit to be done as soon as might be, that thereby they might renew their Covenant with, and profess their subjection to that God by whose help alone they could expect Success in their great and difficult enterprise.</ns0:note> Joshua built an altar <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">To wit, for the Offering of Sacrifices, as appears from the follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing verse, and from <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 27. 5, 6, 7.</ns0:note> unto the LORD God of Israel in mount Ebal <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Why not on Mount <ns0:hi>Gerizim</ns0:hi> also? <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> Because Gods Altar was to be but in one place, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 12. 13, 14. and this place was appointed to be Mount <ns0:hi>Ebal, Deut.</ns0:hi> 27. 4, 5. which also seems most proper for it, that in that place whence the Curses of the Law were denounced against Sinners, there might also be the tokens and means of Grace, and Peace, and Reconciliation with God, for the removing of the Curses, and the procuring of Gods Bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing unto Sinners.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 As Moses the servant of the LORD command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed the children of Israel, as it is written in the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 20. 2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>. Deut. 27. 5.</ns0:note> book of the law of Moses, an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> iron; and they offe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red thereon burnt-offerings unto the LORD, and sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crificed peace-offerings.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="32">32 And he wrote there upon the stones <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Not upon the Stones of the Altar, which were to be rough and unpolished, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31. but upon other Stones, sinooth and plaistered, as is manifest from <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 27. 2.</ns0:note> a copy of the law of Moses <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Not certainly the whole five Books of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> for what Stones and time would have sufficed for this! nor the Blessings and the Cur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses here following, which never are, nor can without great impropriety be called <ns0:hi>the Law of Moses,</ns0:hi> seeing they presuppose the Law, and the Observation or Transgression thereof, to which they belong, only as rewards of the one, and punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments of the other: but the most weighty and substantial parts of the Law, as may be gathered from the Laws which are mentioned, and to the violaters whereof the Curses are applied, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 27. 15. &c. and especially the Law of the Ten Commandments.</ns0:note>, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="33">33 And all Israel <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The whole Congregation, old and young, male and female, as it follows, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 35.</ns0:note>, and their elders, and officers, and their judges stood on this side the ark, and on that side <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Some on one side of it, and some on the other.</ns0:note> before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the LORD, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them: half of them over against mount Gerizim <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">These two places were in the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Ephraim,</ns0:hi> not far from <ns0:hi>Shechem,</ns0:hi> as appears both from Scripture, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 11. 29, 30. and 27. 12. <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 9. 7. and from other Authors who lived in those parts, as <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Doctors.</ns0:note>, and half of them over against mount Ebal, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 11. 29<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and 27. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded before, that they should bless <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Or Curse, which is easily understood out of the following verse, and from <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 27. 13, &c.</ns0:note> the people of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="34">34 And afterward <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">After the Altar was built, and the Stones plaistered and writ upon.</ns0:note> he read <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> He commanded the Priests or <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> to read, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 27. 14.</ns0:note> all the words of the law, the blessings and cursings <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Which words come in not by way of Explication, as if the words of the Law were nothing else besides the Blessings and Curses; but by way of addition, to note that these were read over and above the words of the Law.</ns0:note>, according to all <ns0:hi>that is</ns0:hi> written in the book of the law <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">He saith not, <ns0:hi>according to all that was writ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten upon those Stones,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>in the Book of the Law,</ns0:hi> which shews the mistake of them that think the same things were both read and written upon these Stones.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> walked.</ns0:note> were conversant among them <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Who were Proselytes, for no others can be supposed to be with them at this time.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
